markdown_report:
The best initial experiment remains **attribute-sensitive HSTU with a conservative negative curriculum**, evaluated through staged ablations. It targets broad-but-unspecific recommendations and overlooked format/connector distinctions, while testing Electronics’ measured separation weakness. Improvements remain hypotheses.

**Insights from the starting point.** (1) Electronics negatives beat positives at 10.71% of measured positions; discrimination is a concrete intervention target. These training diagnostics do not establish validation ranking quality. (2) Similarity scores near 0.5 imply average cosine near zero; collapse regularization lacks support. Centered spectra could reveal other representation deficiencies. (3) Users report insufficient specificity and compatibility mismatches. Available text offers partial evidence, not reliable proof of compatibility or fulfilled needs.

**Insights from related work.** (1) Official HSTU uses normalized sampled cross-entropy with 128 per-position negatives and temperature 0.05 [1]. Its replacement sampling differs from the proposed filtered, unique sampler. (2) R²NS motivates gradual hardening [2], while HDCCF highlights false-negative risks [8]. Neither establishes this adaptation’s benefit. (3) MARS motivates attribute-sensitive matching [3]. Unordered pooling loses directional relations; a small CNN offers an ordered alternative [6,7], without guaranteeing compatibility understanding.

The framework has three directions: **representation specificity** → gated text residual; **negative discrimination** → normalized objective and curriculum; **temporal context** → HSTU time biases [4]. All operate within one jointly trained network.

Three candidate ideas follow. Scores are originality/potential/user alignment/model alignment/difficulty, each 0–10; higher difficulty means harder implementation. Each assessment lists benefits and limitations in that order.

| Idea | Scores | Positive assessment | Negative assessment |
|---|---|---|---|
| Uniform 128-negative normalized objective [1] | 3/6/4/8/3 | Established; reusable; may improve specificity; directly tests separation; limited architecture work. | Little novelty; uncertain transfer; weak compatibility targeting; margins can mislead; per-position scoring costs memory. |
| Attribute-sensitive curriculum [2,3], selected | 5/7/8/8/6 | Useful adaptation; extensible; targets specificity and format distinctions; challenges confusable negatives; modular implementation. | Established components; sparse text limits transfer; pooling misses relations; false negatives may hurt; controls and serialization add work. |
| Bucketed temporal attention bias [4] | 3/7/7/5/4 | Native mechanism; contextual promise; targets stale interests; may clarify context; lightweight parameters. | Low novelty; timing varies; inactivity cannot prove satisfaction; separation benefit is indirect; timestamp alignment requires care. |

**Selected algorithm.** Jointly learn item IDs plus a gated, masked-mean token residual from permitted titles/descriptions. Preserve identifiers, numbers, units and direction words; compare ordered CNN encoding only after simpler controls justify it. Build deterministic TF-IDF top-100 neighbors. Use 128 uniform negatives through epoch 20, linearly increase neighbor probability to 0.25 during epochs 21–60, then hold. Both uniform control and curriculum exclude padding, target, known training positives and duplicates. Optimize uncorrected normalized contrastive cross-entropy; naïve LogQ correction is unjustified [5].

Prespecify baseline, objective-only, text-only, curriculum-only and targeted combinations; budget permitting, test capacity and shuffled-text controls. Keep seeds, routing, splits, ≤200 epochs and 200 batches/epoch fixed. Select solely by macro validation HR@10, report every attempt and GPU cost, and preserve final-nonpadding readout, diagnostic interfaces and checkpoint/predictor identity. Validation uncertainty and sampled-evaluation limitations remain material [9,10].

idea.description: Train one attribute-sensitive HSTU per category, jointly learning item-ID and lightweight title/description representations. Evaluate a filtered uniform-negative control against a prespecified warm-start followed by a conservative mixture of uniform and stochastic TF-IDF-neighbor negatives, using one learned scoring function and checkpoint per category.
idea.motivation: Address two observed user failures: broad associations replacing specific preferences, and recommendations overlooking explicit format/connector distinctions. Also test the measured Electronics negative-over-positive rate of 10.71%, negative 10th-percentile margin of -0.0749, and small-margin rate of 16.36%. These measurements support a discrimination hypothesis, not a demonstrated held-out improvement. Text provides uncertain attribute evidence; neither purchase histories nor timestamps establish satisfaction, fulfilled needs or physical compatibility. The revised originality/potential/difficulty scores are 5/7/6 because the components are established, transfer is uncertain, and reproducible sampling, controls and deployment require substantial care.
idea.implementation_notes:
Extend the supplied corrected HSTU without replacing its backbone. Preserve preprocessing seed 0, training seed 42, DATA_DIR = os.environ['GAGC_DATA_DIR'], trial-local artifacts, all four routes, supplied splits, maximum 200 epochs and exactly 200 batches per executed epoch. Train sequentially on one GPU; record all training, diagnostics and failed-run GPU seconds against the shared 43,200-second budget. No pretrained weights, external datasets, hidden test files, other-trial checkpoints or separately fitted inference scores are permitted.

Construct text assets only from host-permitted titles/descriptions. Do not use the generic example's unavailable reviews, ratings, prices, stores or item categories. Use deterministic lowercase tokenization that preserves internal digits, decimals, hyphens and slashes, including 3.5mm, USB-C and DVD-Audio, and preserves direction words as tokens. Encode title and description separately, truncating to 32 and 96 tokens respectively. Reserve PAD=0 and UNK=1; retain tokens appearing in at least two permitted item documents, cap vocabulary at 50,000, and order by descending document frequency with lexical tie-breaking. These are proposed reproducible defaults. Record the tokenizer pattern, metadata scope, truncation and vocabulary in the checkpoint. Use a 32-dimensional token embedding, masked mean within each field, concatenate the two field vectors and project to the baseline item dimension. Set item_vector(i) = item_emb(i) + sigmoid(g) * LayerNorm(project(text_i)), with one learned scalar g initialized to -3. Force the residual to zero for missing text and item 0. Keep input/output item representations tied to this same jointly learned representation. No independent text predictor is fitted.

Pooling preserves token identity but loses order and number-unit bindings. Consequently, the method targets learnable distinctions rather than guaranteeing connector direction or compatibility. An optional later ablation replaces pooling with width-2/3/5 CNN filters, masking padded windows and pooling only valid outputs. Match its trainable capacity when comparing against the mean encoder. Character n-grams are a deferred option for rare identifiers, not part of the primary specification; introducing them requires a separately documented ablation.

Build static TF-IDF neighbors from the same truncated text using the recorded tokenizer, raw token counts, idf=log((1+N)/(1+df))+1 and L2 normalization. Exclude self-neighbors, zero-similarity entries and padding; retain up to 100 neighbors, sorted by descending cosine and ascending item ID for ties. Use sparse, chunked retrieval rather than materializing an N-by-N matrix. TF-IDF supplies training proposals only; it never contributes an inference score. Neighbor construction time/storage and GPU mining/scoring time must be logged.

For each valid supervised position, independently sample 128 unique negatives. For the curriculum, set neighbor probability to 0 through epoch 20, 0.25*(epoch-20)/40 during epochs 21–60, and 0.25 thereafter. For each draw, choose uniform catalog sampling or a uniform draw from the target item's stored neighbor list. Reject padding, the target, every item in that user's complete observed training history, and previously selected negatives. Do not consult validation or test histories for exclusions. After 32 failed attempts for a slot, sample uniformly from the remaining eligible catalog; if fewer than 128 eligible items exist, use all eligible items and mask unused slots. Apply identical exclusions, uniqueness, fallback and negative count to the uniform control. This differs deliberately from the official replacement sampler; do not describe it as an exact replication. Use a dedicated seeded sampling generator, with deterministic worker seeding, and retain family-specific sample_batch behavior for causal sequence construction. The host diagnosis loader's four-tuple remains unchanged; carry any training-only user identity needed for exclusions through an internal sampler interface.

Compute logits as cosine(feature, item_vector)/0.05 and optimize cross-entropy with the positive explicitly included once. Apply this objective only at valid nonpadding supervised positions and average those losses. This is an uncorrected contrastive objective, not an unbiased estimate of full-catalog softmax. User filtering and sampling without replacement invalidate naïve -log(128q) corrections. Score negatives in chunks if required; chunking must preserve each position's complete denominator and gradients. Complexity is O(P*128*d) for P supervised positions. A shared negative pool changes correlations and is outside the primary comparison. Hold the corrected baseline optimizer, learning-rate schedule, HSTU width/depth, dropout and sequence length fixed unless a separately reported experiment changes them. If the corrected baseline already uses any proposed component, mark that component as present rather than claiming it as a new ablation.

Prespecify comparisons: corrected baseline; normalized 128-uniform objective without text; text residual with the original objective; curriculum without text under the normalized objective; and the proposed full combination. Use targeted removals to resolve interactions only if the budget permits. Normalization, temperature, negative count, text and sampling can interact; do not attribute a combined improvement to one component. An immediate-neighbor control can distinguish warm-start effects from simply adding hard negatives, at matched proposal/scoring cost. Sampling objectives already emphasize difficult negatives, making overlap with temperature effects plausible. Never launch an ablation that cannot fit the remaining budget; report omitted controls and every attempted configuration.

Preserve the host's validation schedule and checkpoint rule, specifying its actual settings in the experiment manifest before training. If the baseline supplies no checkpoint tie rule, prefer the earliest checkpoint among equal macro validation HR@10 values. The independently pinned host evaluator remains authoritative. Keep candidate sets and evaluation seed 42 unchanged. Do not select on Electronics alone or on diagnostic margins. With 200 users/category, one changed user hit changes macro HR@10 by 0.125 percentage points. If per-user validation hits are available, use paired within-category bootstrap resampling with 10,000 replicates and a dedicated analysis RNG seed 42; average the four category means in each replicate. Report percentile 95% intervals and discordant-user counts. These intervals condition on training seed and sampled candidates and do not remove optimism from repeated validation selection. Sampled HR@10 need not imply full-catalog quality or fewer compatibility rejections.

Budget permitting, train a capacity-matched ID-only control, a text-length/missingness-only control, and a shuffled-text control. For shuffling, permute text between items within training-interaction-count deciles and text-length quartiles, using deterministic tie rules and a dedicated seed 42; keep missing-text items separate. These controls require retraining: inference-only text removal introduces distribution shift. Inspect validation effects by training popularity, text length and history length, reporting stratum sizes. Track score/embedding-norm associations with popularity to detect shortcuts. A text-neighbor curriculum can reinforce brand/genre shortcuts and select unobserved positives; known-positive exclusions do not eliminate these risks. Do not claim to measure a true false-negative rate.

Keep DiagnosisProbe(view, device), run_full_diagnosis(train_loader), diagnosis_interpreter_prompt(raw_diagnosis), view.model as the actual trained module, and the host ModelView contracts. Preserve item_emb as the ID embedding module; expose the joint representation through the actual model and use predict_score for all operational margin measurements. Clearly distinguish diagnostics of raw ID embeddings from diagnostics of joint item vectors. log2feats(sequence) must remain callable; no timestamp-dependent inference changes are introduced. Where feasible, add separately defined centered item/final-history variance, spectra and effective rank exp(-sum(p*log(p))) with p proportional to singular values. Higher rank alone is not a recommendation improvement. Record negative-score quantiles and observed-positive proposal rejection rates; record gradient concentration only with an explicit definition and affordable instrumentation. Unavailable category breakdowns remain empty/unavailable rather than inferred from unsupported metadata. The interpretation prompt must use measured values and their definitions.

Use the maximum position index whose item is nonzero for left-padded readout, never nonpadding_count-1; handle an entirely empty sequence explicitly using the baseline convention. Save one selected checkpoint/category containing learned parameters, architecture configuration, vocabulary, tokenizer, token tensors and missing-text masks. Training-only neighbor assets need not load at inference. Update the embedded predictor writer with the identical model definition, normalization, temperature, text fusion and routing. Verify that training and reloaded predictor scores agree on the same permitted example before accepting a trial. Each category loads exactly one independently trained checkpoint; no averaging, expert mixtures, independently fitted transition/popularity scores or score fusion. No new training or validation results are claimed.
idea.pseudocode:
Prespecify experiment variants and the host-compatible validation/checkpoint rule.
For each authorized variant, subject to remaining shared GPU budget:
    For category in the four supplied category routes:
        Reset training RNGs to seed 42; retain preprocessing seed 0 and supplied splits.
        Load permitted training histories and supplied title/description metadata.
        Build deterministic vocabulary, fixed-length token tensors and missing-text masks.
        If curriculum is enabled:
            Build deterministic TF-IDF top-100 neighbors for training proposals only.
        Initialize corrected HSTU; retain its optimizer and architecture settings.
        If text is enabled:
            Add jointly trained masked-mean text residual with gate initialized to -3.
        For epoch = 1 .. min(configured_epochs, 200):
            For batch_index = 1 .. 200:
                Sample causal left-padded examples using the family-specific sampler.
                Retain internal user IDs for training-history negative exclusions.
                If normalized objective is enabled:
                    For each valid supervised position independently:
                        p_neighbor = 0 if uniform control else curriculum_probability(epoch)
                        Draw up to 128 unique negatives using the specified mixture.
                        Reject padding, target and complete observed training-history items.
                        Apply bounded-retry uniform fallback and mask unavailable slots.
                    features = model.log2feats(sequence)
                    logits = cosine(features, joint_item_vectors) / 0.05
                    loss = mean_valid_position_cross_entropy(positive_once, negatives)
                Else:
                    loss = corrected_baseline_objective_using_current_joint_representation()
                Update the single network jointly.
            At the unchanged host validation schedule:
                Obtain permitted macro validation HR@10.
                Apply the prespecified checkpoint rule; never use test data.
            Log elapsed training/diagnosis GPU seconds and enforce the shared budget.
        Save one selected checkpoint with architecture and required text assets.
        Run family-compatible diagnosis, retaining measured definitions.
Write working/predict.py using the identical trained architecture and category routing.
For prediction:
    Load exactly one checkpoint for the requested category.
    features = model.log2feats(left_padded_sequence)
    last_index = maximum position with a nonzero item; handle empty input explicitly.
    scores = model.predict_score(features[last_index], candidate_items)
Verify reload score parity on permitted examples.
Report all attempted configurations, macro validation results and available paired uncertainty.
Do not combine predictors or claim unmeasured compatibility/full-catalog improvements.

originality.positive: Combines attribute-sensitive representations and a conservative negative curriculum within one constrained HSTU, with explicit separation of representation and sampling effects.
originality.negative: The components and curriculum principles are established; novelty lies mainly in the benchmark adaptation and controlled integration.

future_potential.positive: Offers a reusable experimental path for determining whether observable item details improve discrimination beyond broad historical associations.
future_potential.negative: Sparse text, unordered pooling, false negatives and sampled-evaluation limitations may restrict transfer; no improvement has been measured.

code_difficulty.positive: A small text residual and static training proposals preserve the HSTU backbone and avoid extra inference models.
code_difficulty.negative: Per-position filtered sampling, efficient scoring, deterministic text assets, shortcut controls and exact checkpoint/predictor parity require substantial implementation and verification.

related_work.title: [1] Official HSTU sampled-softmax configuration and implementation
contributions: Provides a reference configuration with 128 negatives, normalized query/item embeddings and temperature 0.05.

The accompanying autoregressive_losses.py local sampler draws uniform negatives independently per supervised position with replacement; sampled_softmax.py masks target collisions and applies uncorrected sampled cross-entropy.
limitations: Does not establish optimal settings or improvements for these four Amazon categories.
The proposed user-filtered, unique mixed sampler differs from this implementation; no implemented text-neighbor curriculum comparison is established by these sources.

related_work.title: [2] R²NS
contributions: Motivates uniform warm-start followed by progressively harder stochastic negative sampling.
limitations: Hard negatives can impair early learning and include relevant unobserved items.
The proposed TF-IDF-neighbor schedule is an adaptation to test, not an established result from this work.

related_work.title: [3] MARS
contributions: Motivates attribute-aware representations and matching beyond overall similarity.
limitations: Its pretrained language-model approach is unavailable under this task's constraints.
Attribute similarity does not establish physical compatibility or validate a scratch-trained pooled text encoder.

related_work.title: [4] Actions Speak Louder than Words: Trillion-Parameter Sequential Transducers for Generative Recommendations
contributions: Introduces HSTU with gated interactions and positional/temporal attention mechanisms.
limitations: Temporal context cannot establish whether a purchase fulfilled a need.
Published results do not establish gains for the proposed Amazon adaptation; timestamp features require inference-compatible inputs.

related_work.title: [5] Correcting the LogQ Correction
contributions: Distinguishes the always-included positive from sampled negatives when analyzing proposal correction.
Supports separating sampling-distribution correction from false-negative handling.
limitations: Does not identify genuinely relevant unobserved items.
Does not justify naïve LogQ correction for the proposed user-filtered sampling without replacement.

related_work.title: [6] Deep Unordered Composition Rivals Syntactic Methods for Text Classification
contributions: Demonstrates useful text representations based on unordered embedding aggregation.
limitations: Unordered aggregation cannot distinguish identical token multisets with different directional relations.
Text-classification results do not establish recommendation or compatibility gains.

related_work.title: [7] Convolutional Neural Networks for Sentence Classification
contributions: Provides a lightweight mechanism for ordered local token features through convolution.
limitations: Local filters may miss long-range connector direction and number-unit relationships.
Does not establish superiority for scratch-trained HSTU recommendation.

related_work.title: [8] HDCCF
contributions: Documents the trade-off between informative hard negatives and false negatives in recommendation.
limitations: Does not establish the false-negative rate of TF-IDF title/description neighbors in this benchmark.

related_work.title: [9] On Over-fitting in Model Selection and Subsequent Selection Bias in Performance Evaluation
contributions: Explains how repeated model selection can overfit a finite validation criterion.
limitations: Prespecified comparisons and paired intervals do not eliminate selection optimism or substitute for unavailable held-out evaluation.

related_work.title: [10] On Sampled Metrics for Item Recommendation
contributions: Explains limitations of interpreting recommendation metrics computed on sampled candidate sets.
limitations: Does not authorize modifying the pinned evaluator; full-catalog gains cannot be inferred from sampled HR@10 alone.

related_work.title: Candidate Sampling
contributions: Defines candidate-sampling distributions and the role of expected counts in sampled objectives.
limitations: Correct weighting requires the actual sampling design; filtered weighted sampling without replacement is not corrected by a simple nominal proposal probability.

related_work.title: Revisiting Graph-based Collaborative Filtering: A Linear Residual Graph Convolutional Network Approach
contributions: Discusses how softmax-based contrastive objectives and temperature affect emphasis on difficult negatives.
limitations: Does not establish that a separate hard-negative curriculum improves this HSTU benchmark.
Motivates controlling temperature and sampling effects rather than attributing their combined effect to the curriculum.

related_work.title: The Effective Rank: A Measure of Effective Dimensionality
contributions: Defines effective rank through entropy of normalized singular values.
limitations: Higher effective rank alone does not establish better recommendation quality or diagnose a specific user-facing failure.

related_work.title: Enriching Word Vectors with Subword Information
contributions: Provides a character n-gram mechanism that can inform future from-scratch handling of rare identifiers.
limitations: Character n-grams are deferred from the primary experiment.
The mechanism does not establish compatibility understanding or justify fetching pretrained vectors.
